scope: Explicit operator-approved recovery into a new native SDK context in the same Pi chat, not in-place native continuation or a durable executor

verification.kind: Real Pi RPC, production extension and bridge, MCP, filesystem persistence and synthetic tool effects; external SDK protocol replay

red.failure: An interrupted SDK conversation needs an explicit /sdk-recover operation.

checks: Normal SDK-style tool execution and completed checkpoint before fault injection
Kill worker after a synthetic effect but before recording its result
A recovery request during active tool execution does not interrupt it or open a recovery dialog
Ordinary recovery stays blocked before starting another SDK query
Cancelling explicit recovery does not mutate history
Confirming recovery preserves original history bytes and starts a new explicitly identified native context without rewind or resume flags
An SDK initialization reporting an unexpected native session identity is rejected before tool dispatch
Recorded results, missing-result unknown status and image retained; thinking/signatures omitted
Native usage baseline resets for the new context while previous Pi usage remains recorded
Tampered history, recovery decision, interrupted identity, checkpoint binding, changed configuration and intervening input reject before SDK startup
Proposed repetition of the interrupted action requires approval and denial executes nothing
A separately approved new action executes once through Pi
Completed checkpoint and mandatory tool approval survive worker restart
Historical tool-call ID reuse rejects before dispatch
Personal settings remain unchanged

readOnlyExistingSessionPreflight.limit: Preflight only. No recovery decision applied to existing conversations, no native query, and no tool execution.

liveObservation.kind: Read-only Pi/native transcript inspection of the operator-approved recovery and subsequent user message
liveObservation.actualError: API 400 requiring workspace extra usage for third-party apps

checks: The exact native billing response matches the new fixed public message
Real Pi RPC serialized assistant content and errorMessage both identify workspace extra usage
The message directs the operator to the workspace admin instead of login or a new session
Arbitrary native error details do not appear in the public response
Synthetic effects and personal settings remain unchanged
billingErrorFollowUp.limit: This corrects the explanation, not workspace billing. No funding or authentication changes, retry of the production SDK request, or successful live inference.

realRpcRecovery.fixture: Synthetic incomplete Pi history, not an interrupted native MCP callback

qualifiedErrorRegression.checks: The public response reports a restriction on this request and suggests checking SDK entitlement; it no longer claims all SDK requests require extra usage or recommends adding funds.

billingRoutingFollowUp.conclusion: The current SDK route works with extra usage disabled. The earlier response is not proof that paid extra usage must be enabled; request-specific failure and the original long chat remain unverified.

red.failure: Recovered chats must retain normal Pi tool permissions without an extra approval prompt.
SDK history changed after recovery approval. Request recovery again.

checks: A new foreign-provider tool call after recovery approval runs under normal Pi permission policy without a recovery prompt
Completed foreign turns and an exact zero-work stale-approval rejection are imported before the first recovered SDK request
Original approved hashes, checkpoint identity, configuration and interrupted identities remain bound
Incomplete foreign turns and new unapproved SDK responses reject before SDK startup
New SDK tool calls do not prompt after recovery or worker restart
Normal Pi permission denial and required-argument validation still prevent execution
Historical calls are not replayed and duplicate tool-use IDs still reject

liveSdkRpc.fixture: Synthetic incomplete Pi history, followed by synthetic completed foreign text and an exact local guard failure; real SDK inference and Pi RPC
liveSdkRpc.limit: Not a real native MCP crash, production conversation prompt, or physical phone verification.

diagnosticRunExcluded.reason: Pi legitimately coerced numeric input into the declared string type; the invalid-argument fixture now omits the required field.

red.failure: The normal Pi prompt retained the known rejected documentation clauses at the SDK boundary.

checks: Normal Pi prompt retains canonical documentation in Pi but omits the generated index from the SDK append
Global/project rules, skills, appended instructions and late extension/tool guidance survive verbatim
Explicit custom prompts and operator-defined docs sections survive
Unaccounted opaque context rewrites reject before SDK startup
Known zero-work billing and local rejections retry without a checkpoint or extra recovery approval
Provider rejections are not mislabeled as requests never sent to the SDK
Foreign-provider error records remain historical context without tool replay
Unknown SDK failures remain blocked
The next user request can restore a closed bridge within the same Pi worker
Old-format checkpoints require confirmed sdk-recover and a new native context
Migrated checkpoints resume normally after a worker restart
Existing argument validation, permission denial, interruption, history and duplicate-ID guards still pass

liveMobile.fixture: Real Pi RPC, SDK Opus, isolated local host and mobile Chromium; synthetic read-only probe
liveMobile.limit: Isolated configuration, not the installed opentunnel host or physical Safari.

productionInstallation.fixture: Installed opentunnel host, normal Pi resources, real SDK Opus and mobile Chromium
productionInstallation.limit: Only the fresh scratch conversation ran inference; no production conversation was recovered and physical Safari was not tested.

limits: Requires Pi's structured prompt-options and transcript-sections API; verified with Pi 1.2.0 and 1.3.0
Opaque inherited Pi base prompts must be made portable by their caller; arbitrary subagent inheritance is not implemented
The upstream content-sensitive rejection remains reproducible through the direct SDK reproduction
No original conversation was rewritten, recovered or used for diagnostic model requests
Initial protocol replay used no inference. portablePromptFollowUp records installed-host normal-resource acceptance; the original long chat and real native MCP crash recovery remain unverified
A valid saved completed checkpoint and unchanged configuration are required
Summary and terminal-command context are unsupported by this recovery operation
Only Pi-saved history enters the new context; unobserved SDK-only state is not resumed and previous transcripts retain their existing retention policy
No general durable executor, automatic completion-receipt reconstruction, power-loss acceptance, unit tests, full local suite or physical Safari verification
